context.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides self-service portals, circulation management, and cataloguing for public and academic libraries. It guarantees EU-only data residency and meets strict performance SLAs for search.

## Key Elements
* **Library Patrons & Staff:** Actors interacting via HTTPS/TLS.
* **Library Management System:** Core software system boundary.
* **EU-Hosted Cloud Infrastructure:** AWS Frankfurt/Dublin region-pinned deployment environment.
* **Third-Party Digital Content Providers:** External system integrated via REST APIs.
* **Payment Gateway:** External system for processing fines and fees.
* **Notification Service:** External system for patron alerts via Webhooks/SMTP.
* **EU-edge Reverse Proxy:** Edge-caching and CDN layer with WAF and rate limiting.

## Relationships
* **Patrons/Staff to Edge Proxy:** HTTPS/TLS 1.3, OIDC/OAuth2 authentication (with MFA for staff).
* **System to Content Providers:** REST/JSON over HTTPS with circuit breakers and fallback caching.
* **System to Payment Gateway:** HTTPS/REST for secure financial transactions.
* **System to Notification Service:** Webhooks/SMTP with HMAC cryptographic message signing.

## Technology Stack
* **AWS Frankfurt/Dublin:** Region-pinned cloud infrastructure to enforce EU-only data residency.
* **OIDC/OAuth2:** Perimeter authentication protocol for all actors.
* **TLS 1.3 / mTLS:** Transport encryption protocols across all context boundaries.
* **EU-edge Reverse Proxy:** CDN and caching layer for static assets and search queries to achieve <800ms 99th-percentile SLA (R-05).

## Rationale
The architecture strictly enforces EU data residency and robust security controls through regional cloud pinning and TLS/OAuth2 standards. Distributed tracing, edge caching, and circuit-breaker patterns ensure high availability and meet the sub-800ms search performance requirement.

## Overview
The Library Management System provides self-service portals, circulation management, and cataloguing for public and academic libraries. It ensures strict EU data residency and high-performance search capabilities.

## Key Elements
- Library Patrons & Staff
- EU-edge Reverse Proxy
- Self-Service Web App
- Admin/Staff Portal
- API Gateway
- Circulation & Cataloguing Service
- Core Search Engine
- Database
- Third-Party Digital Content Providers
- Payment Gateway
- Notification Service

## Relationships
- Library Patrons & Staff -> EU-edge Reverse Proxy (HTTPS/TLS 1.3, OIDC/OAuth2)
- EU-edge Reverse Proxy -> Self-Service Web App / Admin/Staff Portal (HTTPS)
- Self-Service Web App & Admin/Staff Portal -> API Gateway (HTTPS/REST with JWT)
- API Gateway -> Circulation & Cataloguing Service (gRPC/Internal, mTLS)
- Circulation & Cataloguing Service -> Core Search Engine (TCP)
- Circulation & Cataloguing Service -> Database (PostgreSQL Wire Protocol)
- Library Management System -> Third-Party Digital Content Providers (REST/JSON over HTTPS)
- Library Management System -> Payment Gateway (HTTPS/REST)
- Library Management System -> Notification Service (Webhooks/SMTP with HMAC)

## Technology Stack
- React/Next.js SPA & React Admin SPA: Frontend UI deployed on EU-edge static hosting
- Nginx/Kong: API Gateway for routing, rate limiting, and OAuth2/OIDC token validation
- Node.js/TypeScript: Circulation & Cataloguing Service for core business logic
- Elasticsearch: Core Search Engine hosted in EU regions to satisfy R-05 search SLA (<800ms)
- PostgreSQL: Managed database with AES-256 encryption at rest in EU region for data residency

## Rationale
This architecture uses stateless frontends and managed EU-hosted backend services to enforce strict data residency and security compliance. Dedicated search and caching layers guarantee high-performance search SLAs for patrons and staff.

Self-Service Web App.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a comprehensive digital solution for public and academic libraries to catalogue physical and digital items, manage circulation, and provide self-service patron portals with strict EU data residency. It delivers secure, high-performance patron interactions, including rapid catalogue searches and fine settlements.

## Key Elements
- Library Patrons & Staff [person]
- EU-edge Reverse Proxy [externalSystem]
- Self-Service Web App [container, React/Next.js SPA with BFF]
- Admin/Staff Portal [container, React Admin SPA]
- API Gateway [container, Nginx/Kong]
- Circulation & Cataloguing Service [container, Node.js/TypeScript]
- Core Search Engine [container, Elasticsearch]
- Database [container, PostgreSQL]
- Payment Gateway [externalSystem]
- Third-Party Digital Content Providers [externalSystem]
- Notification Service [externalSystem]

## Relationships
- Library Patrons & Staff -> EU-edge Reverse Proxy [HTTPS/TLS 1.3, OIDC/OAuth2]
- EU-edge Reverse Proxy -> Self-Service Web App [HTTPS]
- Self-Service Web App -> API Gateway [HTTPS/REST with HttpOnly Cookie-to-JWT translation]
- API Gateway -> Circulation & Cataloguing Service [gRPC/Internal, mTLS]
- Circulation & Cataloguing Service -> Core Search Engine [TCP]
- Circulation & Cataloguing Service -> Database [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol]
- Fine Payment Widget -> Payment Gateway [HTTPS, via isolated iframe tokenization]
- Circulation & Cataloguing Service -> Third-Party Digital Content Providers [REST/JSON over HTTPS]
- Circulation & Cataloguing Service -> Notification Service [Webhooks/SMTP with HMAC]

## Technology Stack
- React/Next.js SPA with BFF: Chosen for rapid UI rendering, client-side caching, and secure HttpOnly cookie session management.
- Nginx/Kong API Gateway: Selected for robust routing, rate limiting, and OAuth2/OIDC token validation.
- Elasticsearch: Deployed in EU regions to meet the 99th-percentile search response SLA under 800ms.
- PostgreSQL: Managed database with AES-256 encryption at rest to guarantee EU-only data residency.
- Node.js/TypeScript: Utilized for scalable circulation and cataloguing microservices.

## Rationale
This architecture combines an EU-pinned edge frontend with a secure BFF pattern to satisfy strict data residency and XSS/CSRF mitigation requirements. Decoupled microservices and an optimized search engine ensure high performance and low-latency patron interactions.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides self-service portals, circulation management, and cataloguing for public and academic libraries with EU-only data residency and strict search SLAs. It utilizes an Nginx/Kong API Gateway to ensure secure, low-latency routing and token validation.

## Key Elements
* Library Patrons & Staff
* EU-edge Reverse Proxy
* API Gateway (Nginx/Kong) with internal components: Routing & Upstream Proxy, Auth & Token Validation Filter, Rate Limiting & Throttling Engine, Telemetry & Logging Exporter, and Request Transformation & Validation Engine
* Circulation & Cataloguing Service (Node.js/TypeScript)
* Core Search Engine (Elasticsearch)
* Database (PostgreSQL)
* Third-Party Digital Content Providers
* Payment Gateway
* Notification Service

## Relationships
* Library Patrons & Staff -> EU-edge Reverse Proxy [HTTPS/TLS 1.3, OIDC/OAuth2]
* EU-edge Reverse Proxy -> Self-Service Web App & Admin/Staff Portal [HTTPS]
* Self-Service Web App & Admin/Staff Portal -> API Gateway [HTTPS/REST with JWT]
* API Gateway -> Circulation & Cataloguing Service [gRPC/Internal, mTLS]
* Circulation & Cataloguing Service -> Core Search Engine [TCP]
* Circulation & Cataloguing Service -> Database [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol]

## Technology Stack
* Nginx/Kong: Powers the API Gateway for routing, rate limiting, and OAuth2/OIDC token validation.
* Redis: High-availability clustered data store for distributed rate-limiting counters.
* Node.js/TypeScript: Implements the Circulation & Cataloguing Service.
* Elasticsearch: Core Search Engine hosted in EU regions to meet the R-05 search SLA (<800ms).
* PostgreSQL: Managed database with AES-256 encryption at rest to enforce EU-only data residency.
* OpenTelemetry: Emits structured access logs, metrics, and distributed traces via OTLP/gRPC.

## Rationale
This architecture enforces strict EU data residency and robust security controls at the API Gateway before requests reach internal microservices. Distributed rate limiting, schema validation, and optimized Elasticsearch integration guarantee high performance and low-latency search SLAs under peak load.

Circulation & Cataloguing Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a comprehensive platform for public and academic libraries to catalogue physical and digital items, manage circulation, and provide secure self-service portals. It guarantees strict EU-only data residency and high-performance search SLAs.

## Key Elements
- Library Patrons & Staff
- EU-edge Reverse Proxy
- Self-Service Web App (React/Next.js SPA)
- Admin/Staff Portal (React Admin SPA)
- API Gateway (Nginx/Kong)
- Circulation & Cataloguing Service (Node.js/TypeScript)
- Core Search Engine (Elasticsearch)
- Database (PostgreSQL)
- Third-Party Digital Content Providers
- Payment Gateway
- Notification Service

## Relationships
- Library Patrons & Staff -> EU-edge Reverse Proxy [HTTPS/TLS 1.3, OIDC/OAuth2]
- EU-edge Reverse Proxy -> Self-Service Web App & Admin/Staff Portal [HTTPS]
- Self-Service Web App & Admin/Staff Portal -> API Gateway [HTTPS/REST with JWT]
- API Gateway -> Circulation & Cataloguing Service [gRPC/Internal, mTLS]
- Circulation & Cataloguing Service -> Core Search Engine [TCP over TLS]
- Circulation & Cataloguing Service -> Database [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol over TLS]
- Circulation & Cataloguing Service -> Third-Party Digital Content Providers [REST/JSON over HTTPS]
- Circulation & Cataloguing Service -> Payment Gateway [HTTPS/REST]
- Circulation & Cataloguing Service -> Notification Service [Webhooks/SMTP with HMAC]

## Technology Stack
- Node.js & TypeScript: Powers the Circulation & Cataloguing Service with structured schemas (Zod).
- PostgreSQL: Stores transactional data with AES-256 encryption at rest and a transactional outbox pattern.
- Elasticsearch: Delivers low-latency catalog search meeting the <800ms SLA.
- Nginx/Kong: Acts as the API Gateway for routing and JWT validation.
- React & Next.js: Provides frontend SPA experiences deployed on EU-edge static hosting.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict EU-only data residency through regional database and search deployments while isolating failures using circuit breakers and bulkhead patterns. The outbox pattern guarantees reliable audit logging and webhook dispatches without risking data loss.

Core Search Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides a comprehensive solution for public and academic libraries to catalogue physical and digital items, manage circulation, and offer self-service portals. It ensures strict EU-only data residency and maintains a 99th-percentile search response time under 800 milliseconds.

## Key Elements
- Library Patrons & Staff [person]
- EU-edge Reverse Proxy [externalSystem]
- Third-Party Digital Content Providers [externalSystem]
- Payment Gateway [externalSystem]
- Notification Service [externalSystem]
- Self-Service Web App (React/Next.js SPA) [container]
- Admin/Staff Portal (React Admin SPA) [container]
- API Gateway (Nginx/Kong) [container]
- Circulation & Cataloguing Service (Node.js/TypeScript) [container]
- Core Search Engine (Elasticsearch 3-node cluster) [container]
- Database (PostgreSQL) [container]
- Query Processing Component, Indexing Component, Search Indices, Analysis Component, Cluster Coordination Component [components]

## Relationships
- Library Patrons & Staff -> EU-edge Reverse Proxy [HTTPS/TLS 1.3, OIDC/OAuth2]
- Self-Service Web App & Admin/Staff Portal -> API Gateway [HTTPS/REST with JWT]
- API Gateway -> Circulation & Cataloguing Service [gRPC/Internal, mTLS]
- Circulation & Cataloguing Service -> Core Search Engine [HTTP/REST over TCP, mTLS]
- Circulation & Cataloguing Service -> Database [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol]
- Circulation & Cataloguing Service -> Third-Party Digital Content Providers [REST/JSON over HTTPS]
- Circulation & Cataloguing Service -> Payment Gateway [HTTPS/REST]
- Circulation & Cataloguing Service -> Notification Service [Webhooks/SMTP with HMAC]

## Technology Stack
- Elasticsearch: Selected for the Core Search Engine to natively guarantee sub-800ms search latencies (R-05) via inverted index architecture.
- PostgreSQL: Utilized as the managed database with AES-256 encryption at rest to enforce EU-only data residency constraints.
- React/Next.js & React Admin: Deployed on EU-edge static hosting for patron and staff frontend applications.
- Nginx/Kong: Acts as the API Gateway for routing, rate limiting, and OAuth2/OIDC token validation.
- Node.js/TypeScript: Powers the Circulation & Cataloguing Service business logic.
- Transport Layer Security (TLS 1.3 with mTLS): Secures internal service-to-service communication.

## Rationale
This architecture uses a high-performance search engine and a managed database deployed across dedicated EU availability zones to meet strict data residency mandates and performance SLAs. Strict API gateways, mTLS, and RBAC secure internal components against denial-of-service vectors while supporting complex cataloguing and discovery features.

Database.analysis:
## Overview
[The Library Management System is a comprehensive solution providing self-service portals, circulation management, and cataloguing for public and academic libraries. It ensures strict EU-only data residency and high-performance search capabilities.]

## Key Elements
* Library Patrons & Staff
* EU-edge Reverse Proxy
* Self-Service Web App
* Admin/Staff Portal
* API Gateway
* Circulation & Cataloguing Service
* Core Search Engine
* Database (PostgreSQL with Connection Pool Manager, Relational Storage Engine, Audit & Encryption Subsystem, Replication & Backup Subsystem, and Data Retention & Archival Subsystem)
* Third-Party Digital Content Providers
* Payment Gateway
* Notification Service

## Relationships
* Library Patrons & Staff -> EU-edge Reverse Proxy (HTTPS/TLS 1.3, OIDC/OAuth2)
* EU-edge Reverse Proxy -> Self-Service Web App (HTTPS)
* EU-edge Reverse Proxy -> Admin/Staff Portal (HTTPS)
* Self-Service Web App -> API Gateway (HTTPS/REST with JWT)
* Admin/Staff Portal -> API Gateway (HTTPS/REST with JWT)
* API Gateway -> Circulation & Cataloguing Service (gRPC/Internal, mTLS)
* Circulation & Cataloguing Service -> Core Search Engine (TCP)
* Circulation & Cataloguing Service -> Database Connection Pool Manager (PostgreSQL Wire Protocol, mTLS)
* Circulation & Cataloguing Service -> Third-Party Digital Content Providers (REST/JSON over HTTPS)
* Circulation & Cataloguing Service -> Payment Gateway (HTTPS/REST)
* Circulation & Cataloguing Service -> Notification Service (Webhooks/SMTP with HMAC)

## Technology Stack
* React/Next.js SPA: Frontend implementation for patron self-service
* React Admin SPA: Frontend implementation for staff operations
* Nginx/Kong: API Gateway for routing, rate limiting, and JWT validation
* Node.js/TypeScript: Core business logic implementation
* Elasticsearch: Core search engine ensuring search SLAs under 800ms
* PostgreSQL: Managed database with AES-256 encryption at rest, B-tree/GIN indexing, and EU region placement

## Rationale
[This architecture cleanly separates frontend interfaces, API routing, and core domain services to maintain high availability and performance. Utilizing managed PostgreSQL in the EU region with strict encryption and connection pooling directly satisfies data residency constraints and performance SLAs.]
